recipes.name: Basic Béchamel Sauce
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon salt, or more to taste

steps.text: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add flour and whisk until smooth. Cook and stir until roux is a light, golden, sandy color, about 7 minutes.

Increase heat to medium-high and slowly whisk in milk until thickened. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to medium-low and continue simmering until flour has softened and no longer tastes gritty, 10 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Basic Béchamel Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Béchamel sauce is a creamy French white sauce that’s used in many dishes, from lasagna to moussaka. It’s also a base for a variety of cheese sauces.

video.description: Making gloriously decadent béchamel sauce at home is a breeze, and this ultra-creamy classic sauce elevates every dish it touches. It's an easy way to enrich pasta, meat, and vegetable dishes in need of some extra creaminess and flavor. In this video, find out how to prepare this classic French white sauce at home from Chef Nicole McLaughlin, and then learn how to make her ultimate mac and cheese recipe.

review.reviewBody: I was comparing Bechamel Sauce Recipes and this is similar to the one I found on Food Network by Mario Batali which I've made before with the exception of an increase in the nutmeg by 1/4 tsp. This recipe is fabulous and I have added a splash of white wine as I used the sauce for Spinach Lasagna. Decreased the salt to 1 tsp. due to the parm and romano I used with the Ricotta in the filling. Wow and Excellent!!

Excellent instruction for those new to this kind of home made sauce base and the taste of this recipe is very good while also easy to spice in different ways. However, still like our family recipe a bit better. I puree a sweet onion until it's literally pulped, then saute the onion in a bit of butter and olive oil or coconut oil (the oil keeps the butter from burning). After the onion has cooked down and out for a good five minutes or so, we add the nutmeg. We put nutmeg is almost everything and the 1/4 tsp called for here is a good amount. Also helps the "onion" flavor to mellow for those who aren't fond of onion (like my boyfriend before I started cooking for him; I began pureeing the onion simply because he does not like the texture of onion and thought he didn't like the taste - now he knows better). After the onion is pureed we add the amount of butter called for in this recipe, or thereabouts, and begin incorporating the flour straight into the onion, all the while mixing and mashing like it up together. The flour and onion mixture will begin to smell a bit nutty and turn slightly golden - this is what ya want. Then whisk in your milk or cream and there ya have it. Excellent rendition of this simple bechamel sauce with a bit more panache.

BASIC BECHEMEL SAUCE RECIPE: The Basic Béchamel Ratio The basic ratio for a classic béchamel is 3 ounces of fat (butter, ghee, coconut oil) to 3 ounces of all-purpose flour for the roux. This ratio of roux will thicken up to a quart of milk, but you can use less milk for a thicker sauce, as we do below. Use Basic cooking sense. Use directions above. Just use your judgement when adding the milk and nutmeg. Start small and add until the thickness and flavor you want is reached. You can never go wrong.

This recipe calls for 1Tbsp of flour per cup of milk, which is the formula for a thin white sauce. A medium sauce would need 2T/cup, and a thick sauce needs 3T/cup. Also, I was taught to heat the milk and add it all at once (Julia used this method). One more note is that the roux needs to cook long enough so as not to taste of raw flour, but if you cook it to a dark color, the thickening power lessens. A lot of New Orleans cooking calls for a very dark roux, because it has a richer flavor in the final dish.

I used the recipe with whole milk and we found it delicious. I added the sauce to my shepherds pie to rave reviews. I used plant-based hamburger meat and the sauce really kicked it up. Simply add the bechamel to the cooked meat, pea, carrots and corn mixture and top with mashed potatoes. Definitely a comfort dish that is easy and affordable and delicious.

Although this was my first time using this recipe, I made three changes. 1. I reduced the amount of milk from 1 qt to starting with 3/4 cup, allowing some time to sit and thicken, then added another 1/4 c (whisking to mix well both times). 2. I also used whole milk not half/half. 3. I added 2 to 3 oz of Cream Cheese - allowing it to melt slowly and whisking periodically to avoid sticking & ensure there were no lumps. Balance of recipe and cooking instructions were kept the same. I recommend and will make again. (Due to spur of the moment dinner choice, I had to utilize what I had in my pantry. Thus, I used elbow macaroni. Although a very good substitute choice, I'm going to try the egg noodles or linguine next time. Good Luck

This was what I used tonight to prepare lasagna. The bechamel turned out absolutely lovely,smooth,thick and creamy. Because bechamel is a delicately flavored sauce I needed to heighten the flavor for use in such a robust dish as a lasagna. Another reviewer JodieNMain advised sauteeing a pureed sweet onion down and adding a generous 1/4 tsp nutmeg before adding the flour so that's what I did and the result was delightsome!

For me, this sauce is too basic. The milk should be pre-infused with onion, crushed garlic & some thyme before adding to the roux. I personally like to add both cheddar and Parmesan to the sauce to take on some extra flavour and texture, particularly when being used for lasagna. It is a reasonable recipe for a basic sauce.

I read the comments about the nutmeg flavor being too strong. I checked other béchamel recipes online and found that most recipes used one of the following measures of nutmeg in a quart of milk: (none, substituting a pinch of pepper) - a dash - 1/16 tsp. - 1/8 tsp. None had 1/4 tsp. When I make it I will start with a dash of nutmeg and work my way up because I can always add more as needed.

We love to make this sauce! You can add a half cup of your choice of cheese and turn it into home-made Mac 'n cheese. There are so many ways to use this sauce, we also use spinach. Try it, you'll love it!

I'm a 67 year old male that has been cooking all his life because both of my parents cooked every meal, every day, usually with all fresh or home canned veggies and meats. It was a fun family affair! The family the cooks together, stays and prays together! The basic bechamel sauce is the first thing any upcoming chef or cook should learn to make. It's the basis for any and all gravies, sauces, roux, etc. If you can master a roux, which you can with practice, you have the beginning for many a good Cajun recipe!

The roux should be equal amounts of flour and butter BY WEIGHT. Giving a volume measurement on flour needs to come with so many footnotes about whether you sifted it, if you spooned and leveled it, or if you just haphazardly scooped it, but you NEVER have to discuss any of these things if you simply give it by weight. Stop using volume for dry goods!
